name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: UKMTO says two tankers were hit by projectiles off Oman's Khasab on 21 Nov, after Iranian mine claims on 19–20 Nov
state: UKMTO reported two tankers hit by unidentified projectiles 11 and 17 nautical miles from Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz on 21 Nov, with no casualties reported, while Iran's navy said a tanker hit a mine in a restricted area (Jerusalem Post, citing Reuters). This follows Iranian claims that tankers hit its mines east of the strait on 19–20 Nov, and CBS News reported continued US and Iranian strikes in the week to 20 Nov. Repeated attacks and mines keep Hormuz traffic materially impeded.
for_you: Shipping, insurance and oil supply through Hormuz stay disrupted, which tends to feed through to fuel and freight costs. Seafarers can follow UKMTO advisories.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by attacks and mines (UKMTO, 21 Nov)

sources.title: Jerusalem Post — Two tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz near Oman, UKMTO says
CBS News — U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
